name: Dalian Zhoushuizi International Airport
before:
The busiest airport in north east China, in Ganjingzi District about 10 km north west of central Dalian. It handled 19,787,716 passengers in 2025, twenty seventh in the country, and is the hub for Dalian Airlines.

The Japanese and Korean links are what set it apart. Japan Airlines flies daily from Narita, Korean Air and Asiana both fly daily from Incheon, and Air China stops here on its Beijing to Japan services. China Southern runs many of its Japanese destinations through Dalian as a focus city.

Getting into the city is easy. Dalian Metro Line 2 serves the airport, along with a number of bus lines, an airport bus into the central district and a taxi hub on the ground level.

The airport has reached its design capacity, and a replacement, Dalian Jinzhouwan International, is being built on an artificial island in the same district.

The name has a history. The site was a marsh known locally as smelly waters, became a racecourse under the late Qing, and was renamed after a nearby village once it was drained.
after:
Dalian's airport, in Ganjingzi District about 10 km north west of the city centre. It handled 19,787,716 passengers in 2025, 27th in China.

A replacement, Dalian Jinzhouwan International, is being built in the same district.
